title: Sorting out problems
goal: Complain about a wrong or broken order, deal with customer care, report a stolen phone, pass on exactly what people told you, and negotiate a fair solution calmly.
intro:
Things go wrong: the parcel comes broken, the refund never arrives, your phone disappears on a crowded bus. This unit gives you the Gujarati to fix it — on the phone with customer care, at the shop counter and at the police station — without losing your temper.

The key skill is **reporting exactly what people said**: **તમે કહ્યું હતું કે ત્રણ દિવસમાં થઈ જશે** 'you said it would be done in three days', **એમણે મને કાલે આવવાનું કહ્યું** 'they told me to come tomorrow', and **પાર્સલ ગઈકાલે આવવાનું હતું** 'the parcel was supposed to come yesterday'.

grammar.title: Reporting what people said: કહ્યું કે, જણાવ્યું કે, પૂછ્યું કે
grammar.body:
Unit 20 introduced **એણે કહ્યું કે…**. When you're sorting out a problem you need to report precisely, so here is the full system.

**Keep the original tense.** Whatever was said keeps its tense after **કે**: 'It will come tomorrow' → **એમણે કહ્યું કે કાલે આવી જશે** 'they said it would come tomorrow'. English shifts 'will' to 'would'; Gujarati doesn't.

**Promises made earlier** use **કહ્યું હતું** 'had said': **તમે કહ્યું હતું કે ત્રણ દિવસમાં થઈ જશે** 'you said (back then) it would be done in three days'. This is the sentence you'll use most with customer care.

**Who said it** takes the ergative (**મેં, તેં, એણે, એમણે, દુકાનદારે, પોલીસે**) and the verb stays **કહ્યું** / **પૂછ્યું** / **જણાવ્યું**. **Who was told** takes **-ને**: **એમણે મને કહ્યું**.

**Which verb**: **કહેવું** 'say, tell'; **જણાવવું** 'inform, let know' (offices and companies: **અમે તમને જણાવીશું** 'we'll let you know'); **પૂછવું** 'ask'. The trap for Hindi speakers: Gujarati **બતાવવું** means 'show', not 'tell' — 'tell me' is **મને કહો**.

**Questions**: keep the question word (**મેં પૂછ્યું કે મારો ઑર્ડર ક્યાં છે**); for yes/no add **કે નહીં** 'whether': **એણે પૂછ્યું કે બિલ છે કે નહીં**.

**Gossip / ongoing**: **કહેતા હતા કે…** 'they were saying that…' agrees with the speaker (કહેતો, કહેતી, કહેતા).

grammar.title: Reporting requests: 'they told me to…', 'not to…'
grammar.body:
To pass on an instruction there are two everyday ways.

**1. Quote the command** after **કે**, in the form it was given: **એમણે કહ્યું કે કાલે આવજો** 'they said: come tomorrow' = 'they told me to come tomorrow'.

**2. Use -વાનું + કહેવું**: **એમણે મને કાલે આવવાનું કહ્યું** 'they told me to come tomorrow'. A shorter variant is **-વા કહેવું**: **મને રાહ જોવા કહ્યું** 'they told me to wait'. The person told takes **-ને**.

**Not to**: put **ન** before the -વાનું form: **એમણે મને ફોન ન કરવાનું કહ્યું** 'they told me not to call'. 'Refused to' is **-વાની ના પાડી**: **દુકાનદારે પૈસા પાછા આપવાની ના પાડી** 'the shopkeeper refused to give the money back' (here -વાની is feminine, agreeing with **ના**).

**Asking for something**: **માગવું** 'to ask for'. It's transitive, so in the past it agrees with the thing: **મેં રિફંડ માગ્યું** (n), **એમણે પુરાવો માગ્યો** (m), **મેં રસીદ માગી** (f).

The trap: don't use **પૂછવું** for requests. **પૂછવું** is asking a *question*; asking someone *to do* something is **કહેવું**, asking *for* something is **માગવું**.

grammar.title: 'Was supposed to': -વાનું હતું
grammar.body:
Unit 13 taught **-વાનું છે** 'is going to'. Put it in the past with **હતું** and it means 'was going to' or 'was supposed to' — perfect for things that didn't happen as promised.

It agrees with the **subject** like an adjective:
**પાર્સલ** (n) **આવવાનું હતું** 'the parcel was supposed to come'
**ડિલિવરી** (f) **થવાની હતી** 'the delivery was supposed to happen'
**મિસ્ત્રી** (m) **આવવાનો હતો** 'the repairman was supposed to come'
**હું આવવાનો / આવવાની હતી** 'I was going to come' (man / woman)

With **મારે** it means 'I was supposed to / had to (and didn't)': **મારે આજે બેંક જવાનું હતું** 'I was supposed to go to the bank today' — the -વાનું stays neuter, or agrees with an object: **મારે ફરિયાદ નોંધાવવાની હતી**.

**About to**: add **જ**: **હું તમને ફોન કરવાનો જ હતો!** 'I was just about to call you!' — the classic reply when someone calls to ask where you are.

The trap: **આવવાનું હતું** (was supposed to come) is not **આવ્યું હતું** (had come).

culture: Customer care lines in Gujarat usually answer in Hindi or English; ask **ગુજરાતીમાં વાત થઈ શકે?** and you'll sometimes get a Gujarati speaker, otherwise people switch to Hindi without fuss. Agents use very polite Gujarati (**આપ**, **જણાવશો?**, **સર / મૅડમ**); you can answer with an ordinary polite **તમે**. What works is calm persistence: quote what you were told (**તમે કહ્યું હતું કે…**), ask for a complaint number, and escalate with **મારે મૅનેજર સાથે વાત કરવી છે** rather than shouting — **બૂમો પાડવી** makes people dig in. At a local shop, Gujarati bargaining instincts help: offer **કોઈ વચલો રસ્તો** like an exchange or part refund. For a lost or stolen phone you'll need a police report (an FIR, or an online complaint on the Gujarat Police site) to get a new SIM; go with a friend, call the officer **સાહેબ**, and expect a few **ધક્કા**. And the warning every Gujarati family WhatsApp group repeats: no bank or company ever asks for your **ઓટીપી** on the phone — **આ તો છેતરપિંડી છે!**

tip.title: -વાનું હતું — was supposed to
tip.body:
- **-વાનું હતું** = 'was supposed to / was going to'.
- It agrees with the subject: ઑર્ડર **આવવાનો હતો** (m), ડિલિવરી **થવાની હતી** (f), પાર્સલ **આવવાનું હતું** (n).
- With **જ**: હું ફોન કરવાનો **જ** હતો 'I was just about to call'.
- Not the same as **આવ્યું હતું** 'had come'.

lessons.title: Calling customer care

tip.title: On the phone with customer care
tip.body:
- Agents use formal Gujarati: **આપ**, **સર / મૅડમ**, **જણાવશો?** You can answer with a normal polite **તમે**.
- Say what you want: **મને રિફંડ જોઈએ છે** · **મેં રિફંડ માગ્યું**.
- Listen for the passive: ફરિયાદ **નોંધાઈ ગઈ છે** 'has been registered' (Unit 31).

lessons.title: What exactly did they say?

tip.title: કહ્યું હતું કે… — what you were told
tip.body:
- After **કહ્યું કે / જણાવ્યું કે / પૂછ્યું કે** keep the original tense: … કે કાલે **આવી જશે**.
- An earlier promise: **તમે કહ્યું હતું કે** ત્રણ દિવસમાં થઈ જશે.
- Yes/no questions: **… કે નહીં** 'whether'.
- Gujarati **બતાવવું** = show; 'tell' is **કહેવું**.

new: તમે કહ્યું હતું કે ત્રણ દિવસમાં થઈ જશે.

lessons.title: A stolen phone and the police

tip.title: They told me to…
tip.body:
- Quote the command: એમણે કહ્યું કે **કાલે આવજો**.
- Or **-વાનું કહ્યું**: એમણે મને કાલે **આવવાનું** કહ્યું. Shorter: **આવવા** કહ્યું.
- Not to: **ન** + -વાનું. Refused to: **-વાની ના પાડી**.
- Asking *for* something is **માગવું**, not પૂછવું.

lessons.title: Keeping calm and finding a solution

tip.title: Cool heads win
tip.body:
- Calm it down: **બૂમો ના પાડો**, **શાંતિથી વાત કરીએ**.
- Not your fault: **એમાં મારો કોઈ વાંક નથી**; someone else's: **X-ની બેદરકારી છે**.
- Offer a deal: **કોઈ વચલો રસ્તો કાઢીએ** (કાઢવું 'take out, find').
- Explain: **હું સમજાવું** 'let me explain'.

sentences.roman: gusso karvāthī ukel nahīṃ āve.
sentences.en: Getting angry won't solve anything.

sentences.en: Your carelessness has cost me. (lit. my loss happened)

tip.title: Cheated
tip.body:
- **છેતરવું** 'to cheat': the past agrees with the person cheated: એણે મને **છેતર્યો** (man) / **છેતરી** (woman).
- 'Got conned' uses the passive: હું **છેતરાઈ ગયો / ગઈ**.
- **નકલી** 'fake' never changes. Shout it out: **આ તો છેતરપિંડી છે!**

sentences.native: દુકાનદારે કહ્યું હતું કે એક વર્ષની ગૅરંટી છે.

sentences.native: ગૅરંટીમાં છે, તો પૈસા કેમ માગો છો?
sentences.roman: geranṭīmāṃ chhe, to paisā kem māgo chho?
sentences.en: It's under guarantee, so why are you asking for money?

sentences.native: હું છેતરાઈ ગઈ, આ બૂટ નકલી છે.
sentences.roman: huṃ chhetarāī gaī, ā būṭ naklī chhe.
sentences.en: I got conned, these shoes are fake. (woman speaking)

sentences.native: એમણે કહ્યું કે ઓટીપી આપો, તો રિફંડ આવી જશે.
sentences.roman: emṇe kahyuṃ ke oṭīpī āpo, to rifanḍ āvī jashe.
sentences.en: They said give them the OTP and the refund would come through.

sentences.native: બેંક ક્યારેય ફોન પર ઓટીપી નથી માગતી.
sentences.roman: beṅk kyārey fon par oṭīpī nathī māgtī.
sentences.en: A bank never asks for an OTP over the phone.

sentences.native: રકમ ખાતામાંથી કપાઈ ગઈ, પણ ઑર્ડર નથી આવ્યો.
sentences.roman: rakam khātāmāṃthī kapāī gaī, paṇ orḍar nathī āvyo.
sentences.en: The amount's been taken from my account, but the order hasn't come.

sentences.native: આટલી મોટી રકમ કોઈને ઑનલાઇન ના મોકલાય.
sentences.roman: āṭlī moṭī rakam koīne onlāin nā moklāy.
sentences.en: You shouldn't send such a big amount to anyone online.
